text.p: Texas Rangers designated hitter Mickey Tettleton, coming off knee surgery and batting just .091, announced his retirement Sunday.

The powerful, switch-hitting Tettleton, 36, came off the disabled list June 23 after sitting out five weeks following arthroscopic surgery on his left knee, but was just 4-for-44 this season with three homers and four RBI in 17 games.

"Being the team player that he is, Mickey realised that we were facing some difficult roster decisions," said general manager Doug Melvin. "While we were agonizing over this situation, he stepped forward and made this decision.
"We thank him for the outstanding contributions he has made to this franchise."
Last season, Tettleton batted .246 with 24 homers and 83 RBI in 143 games.
Tettleton, who got the nickname Fruit Loops after crediting daily helpings of the breakfast cereal for his breakout power-hitting year in 1989, played previously for Oakland, Baltimore and Detroit.

Tettleton, who began his career as a catcher and also saw time in the outfield and at first base, leaves the game with 245 home runs. He topped the 20-homer mark six times in his career and four times he hit at least 31.
